skinTears.note: Unchanged by T3D-32C's caps, exactly as it was unchanged by T3D-12B's verdict: the figure is the paddle row against the chest in Sprint, nowhere near the mouth, and it is the same 7.00x the era-wide table in CLAUDE.md records. The caps are part of the halves they close and ride the same weight field as the skin round them, so the mouth region reads 1.02x/1.03x -- the mouth opening rather than anything stretching.

gapeSolid.tool: /opt/blender/blender -b --factory-startup --python tools/triassic/gape-solid.py -- dinocephalosaurus Bite@0.133 Attack@0.367 Heavy@0.5 Eat@0.233 NeckStrike@0.567 [--as-drawn]
gapeSolid.shotsAre: the peak jaw rotation of each clip, measured off the packaged rig (skull-to-jaw angle per frame)
gapeSolid.verdict: PASS -- 0 through and 0 opened at every shot, plain and as drawn
gapeSolid.asDrawnIsTheOneThatCounts: The runtime hides everything src/shared/oral-geometry.ts matches, and this head's Seated jaw hinge tissue was one of them, so the plain run was proving a body the game does not draw.
gapeSolid.note: T3D-12B's three renders were right about the *lining*: the sac closed nothing the seated hinge tissue was not already closing. What nobody asked was whether the hinge tissue is drawn, and it is not -- so as drawn this head stood open at the hinge, 120 px through and 197 opened at Heavy. T3D-32C closes the head's cross-section at the hinge with its own vertices (T.cap_cut) and spans what is left of each half's boundary and domes it into that half (T.cap_mouth), which closes it for the player as well as for the audit. Both parts retired; this head now carries no hidden geometry at all.
